She’s not embarrassingly bad or anything, but the role of exiled magician Prospero simply feels beyond her – this is a giant theatre, a tricky role, and she’s not done any Shakespeare since the ’80s. She’s not a good verse speaker, delivering everything in a concerned-mom monotone that fails to hold this big, weird play together.
This production certainly has some striking moments but far too many underwhelming ones, and if you come out remembering Ariel rather than Prospero, something is amiss.

But it's not enough to save this Tempest. I suppose I must applaud Lloyd for pushing the boat out. But this production is lost at sea.
